issue: Which great sage's curse (उग्र साप मुनिबर कर) lies on the Daṇḍaka forest.
our reading: the great sage, unnamed, as the verse has it
alternatives: Śukrācārya, whose curse on King Daṇḍa laid the land waste (Gita Press English); Gautama (Gita Press Hindi)

issue: बगमेल: riding with reins together, in close array, or with reins let loose at full speed.
our reading: घोड़ोंकी बागें मिलाये / in close array

issue: ग्यान मान जहँ एकउ नाहीं: 'where there is not one (trace) of pride' or 'where there is not one of pride and the other faults'.
our reading: जिसमें मानका एक अंश भी नहीं / not a trace of pride
alternatives: मान आदि एक भी दोष नहीं (Gita Press); ज्ञान और मान — neither pride of knowledge nor honour

review: Agree with the writer: ताड़त here is the act of one Brahmin, not wording about a group, so the literal 'strikes' stands; the owner decides
Agree with the writer: करिबरगामिनी stands next to जनकसुता and reads as Sītā's epithet; as an address to the aged Śabarī it is unlikely
Agree with the writer: बार = देर (a long while) is the usual Awadhi sense with राखे … उर लाई

issue: करिबरगामिनी: an epithet of Sītā (जनकसुता) or a second address to Śabarī beside भामिनी
our reading: epithet of Sītā: news of Janaka's daughter, who walks with the grace of a noble elephant
alternatives: address to Śabarī: tell me, O lady of graceful gait

issue: बहुत बार in राखे बहुत बार उर लाई: बार = देर (for a long while) or बार = time (many times)
our reading: held him to his heart for a long while

issue: ताड़त: strikes/beats, or the milder rebukes/punishes (style §2 milder sense)
